C3 (failed 4/4): ENCODING MISMATCH. In all four rollouts, PF2 is properly revealed by A3 and cited in justification_fact_ids. The settlement's written_summary_due field captures the 3-business-day deadline but never encodes a specific calendar date. C3 apparently expects "Friday, May 17" (per the decisive_facts why text), but PF2's reveal text in every rollout says "within 3 business days of an incident" — it never states the incident date as Tuesday May 14, nor does it compute Friday May 17. The model faithfully encodes the contractual SLA as stated; the check demands a derived calendar date the fact never explicitly provides.

C5 (failed 4/4): MISAPPLIED. PF1 is revealed by A2 and cited in justification_fact_ids in all four rollouts. The settlement's idempotency_enforcement_enabled is true in every case, correctly reflecting PF1's implication. But duplicate_delivery_replay_test_required is true in rollouts 0-2 and false in rollout 3. C5 apparently requires the replay test to be true, yet PF1's reveal text only says the retry worker "bypasses the payment provider's idempotency key on its timeout path" and that reverting config alone won't prevent recurrence — it never explicitly states a replay test is required. The group had the right information but inconsistently concluded whether a replay test was needed. This is a consistent misapplication across all rollouts, suggesting PF1's implication about requiring a replay test is not stated unambiguously enough.

C6 (failed 4/4): MISAPPLIED. PF2 is revealed and cited in all four rollouts. The settlement's affected_enterprise_customers_notified is true in rollouts 0, 2, and 3, but false in rollout 1. C6 apparently requires this field to be true (the plan commits to notifying the two customers). In rollout 1, despite PF2 being revealed and cited, the settlement set affected_enterprise_customers_notified to false while still including a customer_notification commitment targeting Maya. The group had the correct information (exactly two enterprise customers, contractual deadline) but reached an inconsistent conclusion on whether notification was committed. This is misapplied, not an encoding problem — the field name and expected value are clear.

C4 (failed 1/4, rollout 1 only): MISAPPLIED. In rollout 1, PF2 was revealed and cited, yet affected_enterprise_customers_notified was set to false. In the other three rollouts C4 passed with the same fact properly revealed and cited. The single failure is the same misapplied decision as C6 in rollout 1 — the settlement contradicts what PF2 implies despite having the information.

C2 (failed 1/4, rollout 3 only): MISAPPLIED. In rollout 3, PF1 was revealed and cited, idempotency_enforcement_enabled was true, but duplicate_delivery_replay_test_required was set to false. In the other three rollouts C2 passed. This is the same replay-test inconsistency as C5, isolated to rollout 3.
